name: Buserelin

fields.mechanism_of_action: Buserelin is a synthetic superactive analogue of gonadotrophin-releasing hormone (GnRH/LHRH). After an initial stimulation of gonadotrophin release it down-regulates the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis: pituitary LHRH receptor synthesis is blocked and down-regulated, gonadotrophin release is inhibited, and serum testosterone falls to the castration range (Suprefact SmPC sections 4.1 and 5.1).
indications: Advanced hormone-dependent prostatic carcinoma (stage C or D according to Murphy et al.) in which suppression of testosterone is indicated; not after bilateral orchiectomy (Suprefact SmPC section 4.1).
Pituitary desensitisation in preparation for ovulation induction regimens using gonadotrophins (Suprecur SmPC section 4.1).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to buserelin, LHRH or any of the excipients (SmPC section 4.3).
Prostatic tumour insensitive to hormone manipulation, or after surgical removal of the testes (Suprefact SmPC section 4.3).
Must not be given to newborns or premature neonates because of the benzyl alcohol content (Suprefact SmPC section 4.3).
side_effects: Very common: hot flushes, oedema, palpitations, lower abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation, dry skin, acne, changes in scalp hair (alopecia or hirsutism), musculoskeletal discomfort and pain, decreased bone density/osteoporosis, gynaecomastia, testicular atrophy, and decreased libido and potency (SmPC section 4.8).
Common: nervousness, emotional instability, dizziness, headache, sleep disturbance, tiredness, drowsiness, weight change, and increased or decreased appetite and thirst (SmPC section 4.8).

Occasional: anxiety, depression or worsening depression, paraesthesia, memory and concentration disturbance, dry eyes, blurred vision, pressure behind the eyes, facial and peripheral oedema, liver enzyme and bilirubin rises, increased or decreased body hair, and splitting nails (SmPC section 4.8).
Rare: tinnitus, hearing disorders, pituitary adenoma, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, and severe hypersensitivity with shock (SmPC section 4.8).

Injection-site pain or local reaction; transient tumour flare with bone pain, neurological deficit, urinary obstruction, hydronephrosis, lymphostasis, or thrombosis with pulmonary embolism (SmPC sections 4.4 and 4.8).

dosage.adult: Prostate cancer (Suprefact injection): 0.5 mL (0.5 mg) subcutaneously every 8 hours for 7 days, then change on day 8 to intranasal maintenance (Suprefact SmPC section 4.2). IVF pituitary desensitisation (Suprecur injection): total daily dose usually 200-500 micrograms subcutaneously, starting on day 1 of the follicular phase or day 21 in the mid-luteal phase, continued until down-regulation (usually 1-3 weeks) (Suprecur SmPC section 4.2).
dosage.maximum: Suprecur: occasional patients require up to 500 micrograms twice daily to achieve down-regulation (Suprecur SmPC section 4.2).

fields.adult_dosing: Suprefact: 0.5 mL (0.5 mg) subcutaneously every 8 hours for 7 days, then intranasal maintenance from day 8. Suprecur: 200-500 micrograms subcutaneously once daily; up to 500 micrograms twice daily may be needed; continue until oestradiol is below 180 pmol/L and progesterone below 3 nmol/L, usually 1-3 weeks (SmPC section 4.2).
fields.pediatric_dosing: Not indicated in children for the licensed indications; Suprefact injection contains benzyl alcohol and must not be given to newborns or premature neonates (SmPC sections 4.3 and 4.4).
interactions: Antidiabetic agents: their effect may be attenuated during buserelin treatment (SmPC section 4.5).

QT-prolonging medicines (class IA or III antiarrhythmics, methadone, moxifloxacin, antipsychotics): androgen deprivation may prolong the QT interval; assess the benefit-risk ratio (SmPC sections 4.4 and 4.5).
fields.monitoring: Prostate cancer: monitor clinical response, PSA and serum testosterone; testosterone should reach castration level within 2-4 weeks and be checked 3-monthly thereafter. Monitor bone mineral density periodically during long-term therapy. Check blood glucose regularly in diabetic patients and blood pressure in hypertensive patients. Monitor for depression and for disease flare at treatment initiation (Suprefact SmPC section 4.4).
fields.patient_counselling: Explain that hot flushes, mood changes, decreased libido and, with long-term use, bone loss are expected. Advise patients to report new or worsening depression, leg weakness, difficulty passing urine or breathlessness. Effective contraception is required during treatment because buserelin is contraindicated in pregnancy. In prostate cancer, an anti-androgen is started about 5 days before buserelin and continued for 3-4 weeks to prevent tumour flare (Suprefact SmPC sections 4.3, 4.4 and 4.6).
warnings: Disease flare at treatment initiation (about 10%): transient increase in pain, neurological deficit, urinary obstruction or thrombosis; cover with an anti-androgen (SmPC section 4.4).
Increased risk of depression, which may be severe; monitor patients with a history of depression (SmPC section 4.4).
Decreased bone mineral density and increased fracture risk with long-term use; monitor bone mineral density and use preventative measures (SmPC section 4.4).
QT prolongation with androgen deprivation therapy; assess risk before and during treatment (SmPC section 4.4).
Published epidemiological studies suggest an increased risk of cardiovascular disease and diabetes mellitus with GnRH agonists (SmPC section 4.4).
Benzyl alcohol content: risk of gasping syndrome in young children (SmPC section 4.4).
precautions: Monitor blood pressure regularly in patients with hypertension (SmPC section 4.4).
Use particular caution in patients with additional osteoporosis risk factors (chronic alcohol abuse, smoking, long-term anticonvulsants or corticosteroids, family history) (SmPC section 4.4).
If testosterone does not reach the therapeutic range within 4-6 weeks, check adherence and consider alternative therapy (SmPC section 4.4).
Dizziness may impair the ability to drive or operate machinery (SmPC section 4.7).
serious_adverse_reactions: Tumour flare with spinal cord compression or paralysis (SmPC sections 4.4 and 4.8).
fields.pregnancy_guidance: Suprefact and Suprecur are contraindicated in pregnancy and must not be used in pregnant women (SmPC sections 4.3 and 4.6).
fields.lactation_guidance: Buserelin passes into breast milk in small amounts; although negative effects on the infant have not been observed, breast-feeding should be avoided during treatment (SmPC section 4.6).
fields.overdose: Overdose may cause asthenia, headache, nervousness, hot flushes, dizziness, nausea, abdominal pain, lower-limb oedema and mastodynia, as well as injection-site pain, haemorrhage and induration. Treatment is symptomatic (SmPC section 4.9).
fields.pharmacokinetics: Buserelin undergoes metabolic inactivation by peptidases in the liver and kidney, and by pituitary membrane enzymes (Suprefact SmPC section 5.2). After subcutaneous injection the bioavailability is 100%, Cmax occurs about 1 hour post-injection and the half-life is about 80 minutes (Buserelin 1 mg/mL SmPC section 5.2).
clinical_pearls: Start an anti-androgen (e.g. cyproterone acetate 300 mg daily) about 5 days before buserelin and continue for 3-4 weeks to prevent tumour flare (Suprefact SmPC section 4.4).
Testosterone rises transiently and then falls to castration level over 2-4 weeks (Suprefact SmPC section 4.4).
If testosterone does not reach the therapeutic range within 4-6 weeks, check adherence and consider alternative therapy (Suprefact SmPC section 4.4).
In IVF, down-regulation is confirmed by oestradiol below 180 pmol/L and progesterone below 3 nmol/L (Suprecur SmPC section 4.2).
brand_names: Buserelin 1 mg/mL solution for injection (Neon Healthcare)
fields.renal_dose_adjustment: No specific dose adjustment is stated in the SmPC; use with caution in patients with renal impairment because high volumes of the benzyl alcohol-containing injection may accumulate (Suprefact SmPC section 4.4).
fields.hepatic_dose_adjustment: No specific dose adjustment is stated in the SmPC; use with caution in patients with hepatic impairment because high volumes of the benzyl alcohol-containing injection may accumulate (Suprefact SmPC section 4.4).
fields.administration_instructions: Suprefact injection is given subcutaneously at 0.5 mL every 8 hours for 7 days, then changed to intranasal maintenance on day 8. Suprecur injection is given as a single daily subcutaneous injection. Each vial contains enough material for 10 doses; discard after the course and do not use if the contents are cloudy or discoloured (Suprefact SmPC sections 4.2 and 6.6; Suprecur SmPC section 4.2).

notes: The row stores 'Buserelin'. No US human buserelin product is marketed; the DailyMed entry for buserelin is a bulk ingredient for animal drug compounding and was not used. This monograph is sourced from the UK MHRA/emc Summaries of Product Characteristics for Suprefact injection (prostate cancer; product 11242), Suprecur injection (IVF pituitary desensitisation; product 11243) and Buserelin 1 mg/mL injection (product 14105), accessed 2026. Indications, dosing and contraindications differ by product and are attributed accordingly. No boxed warning appears in the UK SmPC. Buserelin is not licensed in the US; US clinicians should consult local labelling.
